narrative: The 2020s saw a vibrant explosion of Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture, driven by the natural hair movement. This social and cultural phenomenon celebrated textured hair in all its forms, from waves to curls to kinks, embracing the inherent beauty of Afro-textured hair without chemical relaxers or heat-straightening. Hairstyles like the afro, cornrows, and box braids became staples of African diasporic identity, while dreadlocks, Bantu knots, and locs were worn with pride as symbols of strength and resilience. Protective hairstyles, designed to shield Afro-textured hair from environmental damage, continued to be a vital part of Black women's beauty routines. With the rise of social media, these styles were showcased on platforms like Instagram, further amplifying their cultural significance and inspiring a new generation of young women to celebrate their natural beauty. As African-American culture continues to evolve, hairstyles have become an essential aspect of self-expression and identity, reflecting a deep connection to heritage and community.
